questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I’ve previously been on a language course in California as well as studying one year at Santa Barbara City College after high school. I always wanted to move back to California, and UCLA has been a dream school of mine every since I visited the campus for the first time as a 16 yo.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy, as long as you follow up on your emails etc. The International Office hosted an orientation day for International students. It was also held a welcome meeting for all study abroad students one evening as well. There is additionaly an online orientation you have to complete digitally. Remember to check you email for invites to all of these things. In general, the American people are super friendly and helpful - so please don’t hesitate to ask anyone about anything, and you will receive so much help!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were tents outside my housing building with people who gave me the room card and showed me where I was located. My roommates helped me find the location to get a Bruin card (school id) and showed me around campus and the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at UCLA’s off-campus housing, which was really easy since you apply through their own housing portal. You are actually guaranteed housing if you’d like through them - either on or off campus, even though you can’t know which one of your approximately 10 priorities you will be assigned. I was assigned the Palo Verde building in Weyburn Place which are completely new buildings from 2022 - extremely nice!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you have to time approx 30 minutes to walk to class.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I received an email from the Political Science deparment that they could guarantee only one course for students like me (in the UCLA system I counted as a third-year transfer student and pre-Political Science major (even though I’m in fact a graduate student). So I received a pte number for the class I most wanted. When you receive a pte number, it let’s you enroll in the class regardless if it says the class is full. Every student get’s a registration date and time, and my experience was that every quarter I received a few days earlier registration day than all of my other 7 roommates. But regardless I was prohibited from enrolling in a lot of popular Political Science classes I wanted because I was only pre-Political Science major, so I had to wait until the second enrollment appointment that comes up a bit later whereas many classes could have filled up. However, I found out that reaching out politely to Professors, they would almost always assign me a pte-number because they think a background as an international graduate student is so interesting they want to have you in their class. This is also the only way to enroll in graduate classes if you want to do that, since your major at UCLA is technically on underhraduate level the registration system won’t let you enroll automatically. 
In the first week or two of classes you can drop classes if you don’t like them after all, and enroll in any other class where a seat opens up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My first quarter the department helped me enroll in that one class I wanted, but the two other quarters I was on my own and the councelor literally didn’t reply until my enrollment appointment was over, so you have to be «on the ball» yourself a lot in the enrollment period.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reaching out to the Professors directly. And please do not miss your enrollment appointment, be on time for registering before the classes fill up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is approx like at home except you have a lot more school work to do than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At KU we are used to only having one exam at the end of the semester, but at UCLA you usually have at least one midterm, a final, and papers and quizzes throughout the quarter. The quarter is only 10/11 weeks and you have at least 3 classes, so you can make the math that there is almost always a test to study for or a paper to write. In my experience the graduate classes were a lot less work in, usually just a term paper. However, you cannot skip the readings! The classes are very discussion based. And for all your subjects, it’s quite impossible to read up just before your exam like is more common at KU. I really liked this aspect of the academics, you quite literally can’t be lazy over there haha.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Law.
International Development: culture, power and development.
International Relations Seminar with Arthur Stein about the decline of the liberal world order.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Foreign Relations of the US.
International Relations Core Seminar with Maggie Peters - about international political economy. 
Peace and War.
International Relations and Technology.
Global studies seminar with Prof. Zipperstein.
International Relations seminar with Prof. Ying about violent non-state actors.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite professors were Prof Chun and Prof Zipperstein - any class with them <3

questions.answer: Daily coffees.. haha

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was in the United Nations Association.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many different kinds, I wish I got even more information about the clubs because the opportunities are unlimited.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take use of the facilites at school. B-fitness and Wooden Center, Sunset Rec etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went a lot to the beach at Santa Monica to tan when I had the time. I also went a lot to the Westfield mall at Century City. Hanging out in Westwood, to get a night-time snack at Diddy Riese cookies or going to in-n-out after parties. I also recommend to travel up to and see San Francisco, and down to San Diego. As well as Palm Springs for the Coachella Festival.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy because I’ve always felt very at home in America with the more friendly culture. Everyone is super interested in you as a foreigner and very helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: When people say «let’s grab coffee sometime» actually hold them up to it and arrange for it by asking later when they are free for it. That’s how I got to know my best friend whi I met in class, and also many other friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Obviously seeing homeless and obvious psychotic people on the streets takes a while to get used to and not freaked out by them every time. I had some not-pleasant experiences in this regard.
Also that the smell of weed is everywhere, it is so common since it is legalized.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness, openness, and warm culture. The daily small talk. The gentlemen culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the cost of UCSHIP at UCLA campus since you won’t be allowed to waive it here.

Be open to people, experiences and many great opportunities will come your way. Say yes to everything (except drugs, hehe).

Enjoy it, it passes way too quick and it is the most amazing time :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Funfacts: To know about the famous undierun at UCLA and the midnight screams during final weeks. 
Also the library is open 24/7 before midterms and finals - I’ve spent many whole nights at Powell Library haha.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I’ve made - many who I know will be my lifelong best friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find anything particularily challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
